title: Licensed tobacco retailer density around secondary schools and student smoking and vaping: a multilevel cross-sectional study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the association between licensed tobacco retailers within 800 metres of secondary schools and students' current smoking and vaping. Design: multilevel cross-sectional linkage of the 2025 school health survey and the state licence list, run inside the survey custodian's secure analysis service. Participants: about 24,400 students in 186 schools. Results will be reported after the custodian approves access.
introduction: Several councils are considering caps on tobacco licences near schools. Published associations between retailer density and youth smoking conflict once area deprivation is modelled, and evidence on vaping is newer and weaker.
methods: Retailers are counted within 800 metres of each school by road network distance and grouped as none, 1 to 4, and 5 or more. Multilevel logistic models with a random intercept for school estimate odds ratios for current smoking and, separately, current vaping, adjusted for school socioeconomic index, neighbourhood deprivation, remoteness, age and sex. The covariate set comes from a causal diagram fixed before the analysis.
results: No analysis has been run; access to the survey data has not been approved. The report will give adjusted odds ratios with intervals for both outcomes and estimates by remoteness.
discussion: Findings will be framed as associations and set against the conflicting published estimates. The discussion will state plainly that the analysis cannot show what a licence cap would do.
limitations: Cross-sectional design; self-reported outcomes; vape-only sellers may be missing from the licence list.
conclusion: To be written. It will describe an association and its sensitivity to deprivation, not an effect of caps.
summary: STROBE-structured draft waiting on data access.
